$schema_note: Hand-curated record of how Hero Siege announces a rare ground drop in chat, for ForgePact#17 (Loot announcements). NOT mechanically extracted (see hs-game-sdk/curated/satanic_zone.json for why curated/ exists). Data only: no binding is generated from this file. Every entry carries its own `status`: `static_reading` (read from the compiled game locally and paraphrased in our own words; no script text is kept anywhere), `inference`, `not_established`, or `measured` (`route.status`, from ForgePact#17's Live procedure 3, and the parts of `chaos_tower_loot_burst` its `live` block lists, from capture forgepact-227-chaos-tower-announce-live-1). `scripts` is the announcement chain by SDK name, in call order. `rarity_key` is the itemInfoStruct key the closure is taken to read: that key "27" holds the rarity is measured (docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md section 16.4), but that the closure reads it is an inference from the codes it compares, because the key strings were not read. `rarity_codes_in_closure` lists every rarity code the closure compares on a branch of its own, and for each whether the online path announces it; the list is what was read, and `announced_online` is `not_established` where the reading does not say. `route` is the call ForgePact's `lootann` ships to show the line offline: `server` (chosen 2026-10-04 after Live procedures 1 and 3; the game's own path, `method`, could not be tested offline (the probe's anon control did not resolve)). The argument is ForgePact docs/loot-announcement-research.md; the shared facts are docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md sections 8.6 and 16.10. `chaos_tower_loot_burst` (ForgePact#227) records how a Chaos Tower floor holds its new ground items in Controller_obj.lootExplosionList until gml_Script_LootExplosion puts them back on the ground at the floor's end (docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md section 16.12), with its own `status` and a `not_established` list.

chaos_tower_loot_burst.read: 2026-10-23, local Ghidra project, the build the decompile index labels 498d588550d8; paraphrased in our own words

live.procedure: ForgePact#227's Live procedure 1 (the research doc's Live procedure 5): research build sha256 a21409cb7320811b8f337cf165f5ec3540cba8ec6a1bc147af68e8f1113a9fa3, slot 14 Sorak, Outskirts of Inoya at Hell, then Chaos_Tower_Floor_01_rm; read through lootannprobe burst, lootann stat and out.txt's lootann decide lines, with the owner watching the screen at the burst
measured: on the first floor, Controller_obj.lootExplosionList read as a reference to an existing ds_list whose size rose by one for each new ground item (4 natural drops before any placement, 1 in the frame of a placed Heroic item) and read 0 once the floor had ended
the listed natural drops' and the placed item's structs (with the list memory on) were built through CreateItemNew in that frame or the one before (burst-fresh rose with burst-listed)
GPV of Controller_obj.lootExplosionGiven read 0 while the floor collected and 1 once it had ended
the floor's end landed the held items: both placed items lay on the ground afterwards, each with the itemTimeStamp it had when listed, and burst-landed read 12

the struct that lands is the listed one, not a copy with the same itemTimeStamp: via=burst (B's announce, burst-landed=12) needs the landed item's key, which ForgePact derives from the item struct's object pointer, to equal a key kept when the entry was listed, and the list held that struct alive in between, so its pointer could not have been reused
the LootGroundInit detour saw each landed item twice (two lootann decide lines per stamp; 12 burst landings for the 6 kept entries); which two calls they were is not established

with the list memory off (the rule before ForgePact#227) a placed Heroic item was decided held-bag-drop at the burst and the owner saw no line; with it on, one was decided announce via=burst and the owner saw its red SERVER line
not_run: a bag drop on a floor (case C); the owner accepted the session without it
the LootExplosion debugger logpoint and the burst-window LootGroundInit logpoints (x64dbg paused the game on its own first-chance C++ exceptions during the floor's fight)
Angelic and Unholy in the tower, the boss room and the lobby, a Wormhole, a floor left unfinished, co-op

controller_variables.name: Controller_obj.lootExplosionList
controller_variables.holds: a plain ds_list of s_LootExplosionData structs, the floor's held ground items, read directly
controller_variables.note: measured that it is a readable ds_list that grows with a floor's new ground items and is empty after the floor's end (live.capture); that its entries are s_LootExplosionData structs is a static reading

controller_variables.name: Controller_obj.lootExplosionGiven
controller_variables.holds: a protected-store key, not the value; the flag behind it gates collection (collect while false) and LootExplosion sets it true
controller_variables.measured: GPV of it read 0 while a floor collected and 1 after the floor's end (live.capture); a direct read was not taken

controller_variables.name: Controller_obj.lootExplosionGold
controller_variables.holds: a protected-store key, not the value; the gold the floor holds until the burst

list_entry.note: itemInstance is the item struct itself, a reference rather than a copy; nothing tests isPlayerDrop before the append, so a player's bag drop on a floor is collected too

scripts.name: gml_Script_LootGroundInit
scripts.role: on a tower floor (room name with the tower's prefix, the IsChaosTower test, or gDataProtected[12] true) outside the excluded rooms, while lootExplosionGiven reads false, appends the new ground item's struct to lootExplosionList unless one item-kind test exempts it; that the call after the append destroys the ground instance is an inference (see not_established)

scripts.name: gml_Script_s_LootExplosionData
scripts.role: the list entry's constructor: itemInstance and isPlayerDrop

scripts.name: gml_Script_LootExplosion
scripts.role: the burst: sets lootExplosionGiven true, drops the held gold, then for each entry calls LootGroundDrop (a new Loot_Ground_obj given the entry's item struct, no CreateItemNew) and LootGroundInit with a second argument true, then clears the list

scripts.name: gml_Script_LootGroundDrop
scripts.role: called by LootExplosion for each held entry; its own body also calls LootGroundInit

scripts.name: gml_Script_anon@1312@gml_Object_Spawn_Next_obj_Create_0
scripts.role: direct caller of LootExplosion; reads chaosTowerFloorFinished, chaosTowerIsLastFloor, chaosTowerFloor, chaosTowerFloorList, nextFloorType and nextFloorNumber, so the burst comes when a floor is finished

scripts.name: gml_Script_WormholeGiveReward
scripts.role: the other direct caller of LootExplosion
